newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia shares dip 1.25 pct as gold sector dives.
newsitem.headline: Australia shares dip 1.25 pct as gold sector dives.

text.p: *Gold stocks diving another 6.4 pct set off broad declines after long record run. Volume 385.76 million, value A$715.68 million, 1,218 stocks traded, 235 steady, 161 up, 822 down

Tumbling Australian gold stocks set off an overall 1.25 percent share market fall, which some dealers said could be the start of a downward correction from an 18 percent rally over the past three months.
"The market has had a very strong run in recent months and quite a few valuations were looking a bit expensive," said John Banos, equity strategist at Merrill Lynch Australia.
The All Ordinaries index ended 33.8 points down at 2,679.2, while September share price index futures contracts fell 43 points to 2,705, a 25.8 point premium to the underlying index.
The gold share index plunged another 6.4 percent.

Today's dive in the wake of new 12-year lows overnight in bullion prices brings the sector's fall to 16.5 percent since last week's news that the Reserve Bank of Australia had sold two-thirds of its gold reserves.

Gold heavyweight Normandy Mining fell four cents to A$1.28, its lowest levels in over four years while the smaller Acacia Resources fell 15 cents to A$1.30, the lowest level since its listing on the stock exchange.
"Nothing is being saved from the massacre at the moment," one senior dealer said, adding investors were bound to start stock-picking in the sector sometime soon.
Among major gold stocks, Newcrest Mining shed as much as 12.5 percent to A$2.64 and Lihir Gold five percent to A$1.84.
Gold may have been at the top of the agenda, but there were few exceptions to the negative trend among blue chips as declines outnumbered advances by more than five to one.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd fell 39.5 cents to end well below A$19 dollars at A$18.855, while WMC lost 30 cents to A$7.84 and Rio Tinto 39 cents to A$22.06.
The interest rate sensitive banks ended mixed. Dealers said there was uncertainty over when another rate cut could happen.

In other local markets, Australian long bond yields hit fresh three-and-a-half year lows following comments by Prime Minister John Howard that he wanted to see lower interest rates, although it was unclear whether he was referring to official interest rates. At 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT) the ten-year T-bond yield was five basis points lower at 6.77 percent.

The Australian dollar was sent reeling and a laborious rally came to a bloody halt for bulls when Howard said rates had come down because of falling budget deficits and that he would like to see them lower still. The currency fell to US$0.7418/23 from US$0.7440/45 on Monday afternoon.
